raw_response:
My wheat went in last October, like I've done for fifty years now. Used the same improved variety seed I bought from the supply shop — the one in the red bag that did fine two years ago. For the whole five mu I put down base fertilizer then, about two spreader-loads of that compound fertilizer, the kind they call "three-in-one." I don't read the numbers on the bag, I just know how far it goes.

Now it's spring and the wheat is up green. I walked the field yesterday with my grandson after school — looks decent, not the best I've seen but not bad. I'll spread some more urea soon when it starts jointing, maybe half a bag per mu. I judge by eye. If the wheat turns yellow I'll add more, if it stays green maybe a bit less. Water — I'll run the pump once or twice more before harvest. Electricity for the well isn't cheap, so I don't water for nothing, but you can't let wheat go thirsty at heading. For weeds, I'll spray once if they get bad — I just ask the shopkeeper what my neighbors are buying. Bugs — I'll keep an eye out, might not spray if I don't see anything chewing.

Harvest will be early June. At my age I can't swing a sickle anymore, so we hire the combine. My nephew helps arrange it. My son will come back from the factory for a couple of days, and my daughter-in-law helps. We need to get the maize in quick — same day or next day after wheat comes out. No time to plow proper, just run the planter through the stubble. Some years I don't even bother with deep tillage.

Maize seed I always buy fresh — hybrid, can't save it. Costs more, about fifty-something yuan per mu. Put fertilizer down with the planter, urea and some compound. Maybe topdress once more around when the tassels come out, if the season looks good and I have money left. Water the maize maybe twice — once after planting if no rain, and once around flowering if it's dry. Maize can take some dryness better than wheat.

Money worries me. Fertilizer prices went up again, and my son's factory work hasn't been steady. I might cut back a little on the maize topdress if things are tight, but I've learned that skimping too much costs you more at harvest. Better to find the cash somewhere. Last year I got about 800 jin per mu of wheat and maybe 900 jin of maize. If I can get that again I'll be satisfied. At my age I'm not chasing record yields — I want a reliable crop that feeds us and leaves a little to sell.
